html:
The Royal Ballet of Cambodia is the classical dance of the Khmer court, performed by dancers in gold costumes with slow, curved hand gestures. Its dancers recall the apsaras carved by the hundreds on the walls of Angkor Wat.

For centuries it was performed in the palace for the king, in rites and to tell tales such as the Reamker, the Khmer Ramayana.

Under the Khmer Rouge, most of its dancers and teachers were killed. The few who survived taught a new generation from memory in the 1980s, and in 2003 UNESCO named it a masterpiece of intangible heritage. See also Sihanouk, whose daughter danced in the troupe.
